mensBasketballFund.name: NCAA Division I Basketball Performance Fund (men's 'units')
mensBasketballFund.howEarned: A conference earns one unit for each game a member plays in the men's NCAA tournament, First Four included and the national championship game excluded. The 67-game tournament produces 132 units a year (First Four 8, first round 64, second round 32, Sweet 16 16, Elite Eight 8, Final Four 4). Units belong to the conference the school was in that season and stay with it if the school leaves.
mensBasketballFund.payout: Each unit is paid every year for 6 years on a rolling basis, so a year's payout covers the previous 6 tournaments. The NCAA pays conferences (usually in April), and each conference decides how to split the money. Most split equally, and some give the earning school a bonus.
mensBasketballFund.covid2020: The 2020 tournament was canceled and no 2020 units were earned. The NCAA cut the total 2020 distribution to about $225M from a planned ~$600M. In later rolling windows the 2020 slot is empty.

unitValueByYear.note: Commonly reported as roughly $2M per unit over 6 years in the mid-2020s.

womensPerformanceUnits.howEarned: Same unit concept as the men's fund: one unit per game played in the women's NCAA tournament, title game excluded. Paid to conferences.
womensPerformanceUnits.growth: Planned to grow each year as the NCAA's women's tournament media value rises. The women's tournament is part of the ESPN championships package (8 years, $920M, from 2024-25, of which women's basketball is ~$65M a year).
womensPerformanceUnits.note: Approval timing and the ~$15M first-year fund are from researcher recall. Per-unit value was not retrieved. With ~132 units a year, a first-year unit would be roughly $110K if the fund covers only the 2025 tournament.

otherDistributions.name: Equal Conference Fund
otherDistributions.description: Equal shares to each D-I basketball conference that meets requirements, including automatic-bid conferences.

otherDistributions.name: Grant-in-Aid Fund
otherDistributions.description: Based on the number of athletic scholarships (equivalencies) awarded. After House, scholarship limits became roster limits, so the formula is being reworked.

otherDistributions.name: Sports Sponsorship Fund
otherDistributions.description: Based on the number of sports sponsored above the D-I minimum.

otherDistributions.name: Academic Unit Fund
otherDistributions.description: Started in 2019-20. Schools earn academic units for meeting APR/GSR/graduation thresholds.

otherDistributions.name: Student Assistance Fund / Student-Athlete Opportunity Fund
otherDistributions.description: Pass-through money for athlete welfare: emergency aid, academic support and travel.

otherDistributions.name: Academic Enhancement Fund
otherDistributions.description: Equal per-school grants for academic support.

otherDistributions.name: House settlement deduction
otherDistributions.description: From 2025-26, about 59-60% of the $2.576B House back-damages (~$1.6B) comes out of NCAA distributions to conferences over 10 years (see house_settlement.json).

otherDistributionsNotes: Total NCAA D-I revenue distribution is roughly $650-750M a year in the mid-2020s, with the Basketball Performance Fund the largest single piece (~35-40%). These are researcher estimates, not verified this session.
